title: Bank Loan Approval Assistant
description: An AI assistant that drafts loan decisions and explains them to applicants and staff.
business_goal: Speed up loan underwriting and provide plain-language explanations of decisions.
users: Loan officers and support staff (about 120 users), plus public-facing chat.

architecture.name: Users
architecture.purpose: Loan officers use the assistant internally while applicants reach it through public chat.
security_considerations: Public chat is a different threat model than internal use
architecture.attack_surface: The public interface invites abuse that internal users would not attempt.

architecture.name: Banking App
architecture.purpose: Web portal and chat widget for loan applications and decision explanations.
security_considerations: Rate limits are not applied to chat
architecture.attack_surface: An unauthenticated user can query the assistant repeatedly.

architecture.name: AI Gateway
architecture.purpose: Entry point that routes requests and enforces policy between the app and the model.
architecture.attack_surface: Policy is only a routing rule, so nothing stops abusive or sensitive requests.

architecture.name: LLM
architecture.purpose: Drafts loan decisions and produces applicant-facing explanations.
security_considerations: Model may expose other applicants' data in rare cases
architecture.attack_surface: An attacker prompts the model to reveal decision logic or protected data.

architecture.name: Policy Store
architecture.purpose: Holds lending policies and past decision examples used as context.
architecture.attack_surface: Retrieval surfaces a similar customer's financial data.

architecture.name: Financial Records
architecture.purpose: Applicant statements, credit reports, and income data pulled into the prompt.
architecture.attack_surface: Every prompt is a potential disclosure of financial data.

architecture.name: Decision Logging
architecture.purpose: Records every decision and explanation for regulatory audit.
security_considerations: Logs are evidence, not just telemetry
architecture.attack_surface: Poorly protected logs expose the same financial data as the system.

architecture.name: Fairness Monitoring
architecture.purpose: Checks whether decisions treat applicants consistently.
architecture.attack_surface: Unfair patterns persist silently and become a legal exposure.

threats.name: Financial data in prompts
threats.description: Full financial statements and credit data are sent to the model for every request.
threats.business_consequences: Regulatory breach, fraud risk, and severe reputational damage for a bank.

threats.name: Unlimited public chat abuse
threats.description: The public interface has no rate limits, so anyone can probe or overload the assistant.
threats.business_consequences: Cost abuse, service degradation, and a playground for attackers.

threats.name: Unfair loan decisions
threats.description: The model reflects historical lending bias in the decisions it drafts.
threats.business_consequences: Discrimination complaints, regulatory action, and public backlash.

threats.name: Prompt injection via chat
threats.description: A user crafts a chat message that overrides the assistant's instructions.
threats.business_consequences: The assistant can be made to reveal data or give dangerous advice.

threats.name: Missing access control
threats.description: Any staff member can see decision context for applicants outside their team.
threats.business_consequences: Financial details of customers are visible to the wrong employees.

threats.name: Wrong explanations
threats.description: The model explains a decision with reasons that contradict the actual underwriting logic.
threats.business_consequences: Customers are misled and the bank's reasoning is not defensible in disputes.

threats.name: Overload of the assistant
threats.description: Automated traffic floods the chat interface and blocks genuine applicants.
threats.business_consequences: Applicants cannot reach support at critical moments.

teaching_points: A public-facing AI has a larger attack surface than an internal one.
Rate limiting is a security control, not just a cost control.
Explaining a loan decision wrongly is a legal risk, not only a product bug.
Financial data in every prompt multiplies the impact of a single mistake.
